payload.matrix_runs:
ONE run, degenerate by construction and recorded as such. Datum: the strongest viable rival, which is the lane shipped today - not a hypothetical, since it is what the engine does now. Candidate: 1a+2a+3a+4a+5a+6a.

Run 1: C1 the owner is reached - datum FAILS the veto twice over (an action URL the phone refuses, and nothing published when the pairing changed after startup), candidate PASSES (absolute URLs accepted by the relay in probe A6, configuration read at announce time, summons fires even when the brief fails). C2 readable +1. C3 host learns nothing PASS versus a datum that passes only by hosting nothing at all. C4 failure visible - datum FAILS, candidate PASSES. C5 +0, same store and relay. Net: two veto failures on the datum, no minuses anywhere.

No second run: a second run needs a surviving rival to promote to datum, and there is none - all twelve alternatives were eliminated at M5 on stated failures. Running the matrix against itself would manufacture the appearance of convergence.

SENSITIVITY: robust, and not because the weights are kind. The datum fails two VETO criteria, so no reweighting of C2, C3 or C5 can flip it. The only checkmark that would matter is not a weight at all - it is the goal system's ruled priority that reaching the owner outranks richness. If that were reversed, aborting the announcement when the brief fails (option 4b) would become defensible. The owner ruled it the other way, and today's failure is the argument for that ruling.
payload.winner:
Winner: the ruled design - key in the URL fragment; ciphertext plus inline decryptor in one self-contained page; notify only after confirming the page serves; degrade to a two-action card and record the failure when it does not; absolutize the answer topic against its base at send time; and let the caller state that a human will adjudicate.

WHY BEYOND THE ARITHMETIC. First, the arithmetic is not what decides it: the datum fails two veto criteria, which is disqualification, and the qualitative reason is that today's lane can appear to work while reaching nobody. Second, every mechanic in the winning column has now been executed against the real services rather than reasoned about - which is the specific discipline whose absence caused this iteration. Third, the ordering was chosen for the failure case rather than the success case: the brief pipeline sits entirely before the summons and is allowed to fail, so the worst outcome is a plainer card rather than a silent gate. Fourth, it is a PORT, not an invention - v1 runs this shape and its own comment names the trap that v2 fell into, which is the strongest evidence available that the design survives contact with a real phone.

The honest weakness: with one candidate, this convergence proves the datum is unacceptable rather than proving this design is the best of several. What makes that acceptable is not the matrix but the provenance - the design document ruled it, v1 runs it, and the probes confirm it - and the residue is D1, the one thing no matrix can settle: whether the owner's thumb closes the loop.
